reason: The cited evidence shows that Al/Ti additions to CoFeNi can introduce chemical ordering (E1) and that annealing-induced ordering increases strength in other HEAs (E3), but no evidence is provided for the specific CoCrFeNiTi alloy, the claimed 700°C annealing treatment producing only SRO without precipitation, or the formation of nanoscale clusters that pin dislocations in this system.
premises: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can be prepared as a random solid solution with few dislocation obstacles
Sub-critical annealing at ~700°C induces only SRO without secondary precipitation
SRO creates nanoscale clusters that act as effective dislocation pinning centers
Dislocation pinning by SRO clusters increases yield strength and hardness
SRO-induced strengthening is analogous to mechanisms observed in other HEAs (e.g., CoFeNi with Al/Ti additions, NiCoCr, TaNbHfZr)
